contract: Borrowed private and shared range caches use SharedMemoryCache for retained entry accounting, eviction and optional key leases. Key/pending workspace lasts through asynchronous settlement. Prefetch admits selection descriptors before construction and forecasts retained payload, metadata and concurrent key leases; demand falls back to exact borrowed reads when optional caching cannot fit.
simplification: Removes the independent payload-only private cache implementation. Private caches identify their file intrinsically and use an empty path field, avoiding duplicated caller paths. Shared caches retain complete identities. JSON numeric-size forecasting is shared with decoded keys.

Oversized shared key declines before serialization and real Parquet rows remain correct
Both pending identities remain charged through a deduplicated read

compatibility: Private range maxBytes now includes retained keys/directory records as shared caches already do; cacheOptions.memoryBudget is honored. Tiny capacities may disable retention/read-ahead while preserving exact demand. Borrowed transport/output buffers remain caller-managed.
remaining: Custom borrowed metadata adapter memory contracts
Borrowed-path local accounting overhead remains 16–18%; whole-runtime caps unproven
performanceTradeoff: Two alternating fresh-process comparisons show 16.2% and 18.0% aggregate local cold/warm overhead. This is accounting correctness and cache consolidation, not a speedup. Private baseline ignored its configured pool; candidate charges 132524 retained bytes. Both versions preserve identical rows, two cold requests per case, zero warm requests, and zero final charges. Borrowed buffers remain caller-managed; this does not prove whole-runtime caps.
optimizations: Synchronous cache hits release key leases before async handoff; static file identity sizing is calculated once per wrapper. Pending reads retain key workspace through settlement.
